DHAKA, Aug. 19 (Xinhua) -- The central bank of Bangladesh has fixed a ceiling on U.S. dollar trading profit for money exchangers, amid a lingering greenback supply shortage and its appreciation against the country's currency taka.

After a meeting with the Money Changers' Association in Dhaka, Bangladesh Bank (BB) spokesperson Serajul Islam told reporters that no money exchangers in the country can now charge over 1.5 taka against a U.S. dollar while buying and selling the greenback.
